title: Level 3 (Advanced) - B-24
notes:
West leads the ♥2 against 7♥. South wins West's opening trump lead, dummy still has 3 trumps left to take care of South's 3 club losers. If spades are 4-3, South should be able to establish a long spade in the dummy and thus avoid the diamond finesse.

South must time the play carefully. If South begins by cashing the ♠A and ruffing a spade, he will be unable to take advantage of a 4-3 spade break. The play will continue ♣A, club ruff, spade ruff, club ruff, spade ruff, club ruff. North will have a good spade, but the defense will have a trump left and the contract will be in trouble.

South should begin by cashing the ♣A and ruffing a club. The ♠A is cashed next, followed by a spade ruff. The play continues with club ruff, spade ruff, club ruff, spade ruff. North has a good spade as before, but by ruffing clubs first, South is able to finish his ruffs in the closed hand. South can draw the last trump. The ♦A is an entry to the good spade in dummy.
